inputs.share_count_basis: 6,201,222,024 ordinary shares in issue at 28 Feb 2026 and at the date of the FY2026 annual report; basic and diluted EPS are identical (note 11(b): no dilutive potential shares). Held flat: no SBC, no options, no buybacks.
inputs.net_debt_note: Company's own definition (FY2026 AR, Liquidity section): short-term pledged bank deposits + bank balances and cash RMB3,140.5m less short-term borrowings RMB1,966.0m = net cash RMB1,174.5m. Lease liabilities (RMB819.2m current + RMB703.9m non-current = RMB1,523.1m) are EXCLUDED from net debt because the full lease payment is charged inside the flows (treatment B). The RMB300m 'other term deposit' placed in FY2026 (investing) is not in the 3,140.5 and is left out of the bridge as a conservative omission.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2020-FY2026 annual reports: no share option or share award scheme; no share-based payment line in the cash flow statement or staff-cost note (SBC-zero market). EquityAwardTaxes 0.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNYHKD=X 1.1747 from Yahoo Finance at 2026-10-23 (epoch 1792760907), model -> quote direction (RMB 1.00 = HK$1.1747). No dual listing for a parity check; cross-check: the FY2026 final dividend of RMB3.00 cents was declared as HK$3.43 cents (ratio 1.143 at the May 2026 declaration rate), consistent in direction and magnitude. Per-share values are computed in RMB and converted at fx_rate; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are in HKD to match current_price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in RMB, the currency of the flows: 10-yr China Government Bond ~1.8% + China equity risk premium ~7.0% x beta 1.25 = ~10.5% cost of equity; net-cash balance sheet so WACC = cost of equity. The house reference for a China consumer name would be ~9.5%; the extra ~1pp is a permanent, all-scenario charge for the structural brand-principal dependency (Nike + Adidas ~87% of revenue, both free to disintermediate at will, demonstrated by Nike's July 2026 online termination). The specific Nike-online outcome and its possible extension to offline / Adidas are NOT in the WACC -- they are priced in the scenario flows and the 35% bear weight, so the event risk is charged once. Same WACC in all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: the full IFRS 16 lease payment (principal + interest, RMB1,090.2m in FY2026, financing-activities line 'Payments for lease liabilities (including interest)') is charged inside adjusted EBITDA via lease_cost_pct_path, and lease liabilities (RMB1,523.1m) are excluded from net debt. EBITDA in the Metrics CSV (RMB2,815.9m) is post-IFRS-16 (D&A of 1,294.1 includes 912.1 ROU depreciation), so ebitda_margin_path is the pre-lease margin and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (PP&E 366.4 + intangibles 15.6 = 382.0, 1.48% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in the cash-tax EBIT. Variable concessionaire fees (RMB1,971.3m) are already in opex.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are nil at 28 Feb 2026 (RMB0.2m at FY2025, share of loss RMB1.8m in FY2026); no NCI adjustment.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (owner_fcf_dcf_component), 10-year horizon, routed per dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical' with the adaptations file applied (RMB WACC, lease treatment B, SBC-zero, CNY/HKD dual currency). First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). OWNER FCF FY2026 = reported FCF 2,444.4 (OCF 2,728.4 - capex 284.0) - interest income 79.5 - lease payments 1,090.2 = RMB1,274.7m; the interest income is stripped because the RMB3.1bn gross cash is added back in the bridge, and the lease payment is stripped because treatment B puts it in the flows. FY2026 owner FCF includes ~RMB217m of working-capital release (inventory -8.6% YoY), which is why the forward build is done from components with a negative wc_capture. Store count 4,360 (from 8,395 at FY2020). SBC is zero so house and street bases coincide (band_position null). PRICE: HKEX regular close; not an after-hours print. NO H1 FY2027 INTERIM IN THE FOLDER: the six months to 31 Aug 2026 were not yet extracted at build time (the FY2026 interim was published 22 Oct 2025, so an H1 FY2027 release is imminent or just out); the FY2027 driver year rests on the company's mid-2026 voluntary disclosure of a 10-20% sales decline and on the 1 Jan 2027 Nike online cut-off. That interim is the single piece of evidence most likely to move the year-1 and year-2 paths.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr (FY2021 peak RMB36.0bn to FY2026 RMB25.7bn); equity CAGR is distorted by >100% payout ratios and is not a growth signal for a distributor returning all cash
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-2.3%) diverges from revenue (-6.5%) and EPS (-14.5%) by more than 30%: book value is flattered by the IPO-era equity base and dividends above earnings; revenue is the governing series. Owner-FCF CAGRs are on the lease- and interest-adjusted series (FY2021 1,961.6; FY2023 2,409.1; FY2026 1,274.7).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (-19.1%) is well below the reported-FCF 3yr CAGR (-15.1%) even with zero SBC: lease payments have fallen slower than cash generation, so a growing share of reported FCF is the IFRS 16 financing-line artefact. CAGR window FY2023->FY2026 for 3yr and FY2021->FY2026 for 5yr.

base.growth_note: FY2027: offline/online drift of -10 to -12% (company disclosed a 10-20% sales decline mid-2026) plus two months (Jan-Feb 2027) without Nike online (~22% of revenue x 2/12 = ~3.7pp). FY2028: the first full year without Nike online -- the remaining ~18pp of that stream leaves, offline continues at mid-single-digit decline, partly offset by other-brand/niche-vertical growth. FY2029-30: tail of store rationalisation; flat from FY2031, low-single-digit thereafter as the surviving 4,000-store offline network tracks China sportswear spend.
base.ebitda_note: Pre-lease (post-IFRS-16) EBITDA margin was 10.9% in FY2026, 11.3% FY2025, 15.4% FY2024, 18.7% FY2022. Dips to 9.2% in FY2028 as the Nike online revenue leaves faster than store/personnel costs, then rebuilds to ~10.3% as the cost base resets (AI/store-ops efficiencies, concession-fee and headcount reductions) -- still 1pp below FY2025-26 and far below the FY2022-24 range.
base.lease_note: FY2026 lease cash 1,090.2 = 4.24% of revenue. Online revenue carried no lease cost, so losing it lifts lease/revenue mechanically (4.24%/0.78 = 5.4%); offset by continued store closures running at -12%/yr in lease cash (1,421 -> 1,241 -> 1,090). Net-of-lease EBITDA margin: FY2026 6.7%, base path 6.0 / 4.5 / 4.7 / 5.1 / 5.5 / 5.8 / 6.0 steady -- the mature level is BELOW the FY2025-26 trough and below every year since IPO.
base.da_note: D&A ex right-of-use: 382.0 (1.48%) in FY2026; rises as a % while revenue falls faster than the store-fitout asset base depreciates, then converges on capex.
base.capex_note: FY2026 capex 284.0 (1.10%), down 24% YoY; held near steady-state replacement (~= D&A ex-ROU by the terminal year).
base.tax_note: Cash tax / PBT: 21.8% FY2024, 22.1% FY2025, 20.2% FY2026 on PBT; PRC statutory 25% plus 5% withholding on dividends upstreamed to the HK holdco. 24% on the lease-cost-basis EBIT, which is below reported PBT.
base.wc_note: Distributor with inventory 5,485.9 + trade receivables 1,338.7 - trade payables 403.0 = RMB6.4bn net working capital (25% of revenue). Negative capture: revenue decline RELEASES cash (FY2026 released ~217 on a -4.7% year), growth consumes it. -12% rather than the full 25% because part of the inventory tied to the Nike online channel will be cleared at a markdown rather than converted at book.
base.narrative: Nike online ends 1 Jan 2027 and is not replaced; Nike offline continues on broadly current terms; Adidas unchanged; China consumer stays soft through FY2028 then normalises. Revenue troughs ~RMB17bn in FY2029 (two-thirds of FY2026, half of the FY2021 peak), the net-of-lease EBITDA margin rebuilds only to 6.0%, and the business becomes a ~RMB600-700m/yr cash generator distributing everything. Terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF for a structurally shrinking cyclical retailer.

bull.growth_note: Same Nike online loss, but Topsports is confirmed as Nike's consolidated offline partner (gains stores as Nike prunes smaller partners), Adidas China keeps outperforming, niche verticals (HOKA, Norrona, norda, running/outdoor concept stores) scale, and instant retail / mini-program sales of non-Nike brands partly backfill the online hole. China sportswear per-capita spend resumes growth from FY2029.
bull.lease_note: Net-of-lease margin 6.3 / 5.4 / 6.1 / 6.8 / 7.3 / 7.8 / 8.0 steady -- recovers to the FY2024 level (10.5%) nowhere; 8.0% is below the FY2022-24 range.
bull.narrative: The Nike online loss is a one-time step-down, not the start of a disintermediation sequence: offline Nike terms are settled on current economics, Adidas stays, and the diversified brand portfolio plus a China consumer recovery turn the surviving network back to low-single-digit growth with margins rebuilding toward 8% net of leases.

bear.growth_note: Nike online loss lands at the full ~22% with no backfill, offline Nike terms are reset in Nike's favour (fewer stores, lower margin, Nike takes flagship/high-street locations direct), Adidas follows Nike's online playbook by FY2029, and Chinese discretionary spend stays weak. Revenue roughly halves to ~RMB12bn by FY2033 and does not grow.
bear.lease_note: Net-of-lease margin 5.2 / 2.6 / 2.3 / 2.4 / 2.7 / 3.1 / 3.4 / 3.5 steady -- a thin but positive operating business; the early years are carried by working-capital release as inventory and receivables unwind.
bear.narrative: The July 2026 Nike notice is the first step of a full DTC shift by both principals. Topsports is left as a shrinking offline operator of lower-tier Nike/Adidas doors plus a long tail of small brands, earning ~3.5% of revenue net of leases on half today's sales. Most of the value in this path is the net cash and the working capital that unwinds on the way down, not the terminal business.

scenario_narratives.base: Nike's online authorization ends 1 January 2027 and the ~22% of FY2026 revenue it represented is lost over FY2027-FY2028 with no replacement; Nike offline cooperation continues on broadly current terms and Adidas is unchanged. Combined with the pre-existing offline drift (store count 8,395 -> 4,360 since FY2020, mid-2026 sales down 10-20%), revenue falls to ~RMB17bn by FY2029 and then stabilises. Store, personnel and platform costs come out behind the revenue, so the net-of-lease EBITDA margin dips to ~4.5% in FY2028 before rebuilding to 6.0% -- still below the FY2026 trough of 6.7%. Working capital (RMB6.4bn net) releases cash through the contraction. The surviving business is a ~RMB600-700m/yr cash distributor on a net-cash balance sheet, valued at 10.5% with a 12x terminal cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: The Nike online loss is a single step-down rather than the opening of a disintermediation sequence. Nike consolidates its offline network around Topsports (which already runs over half of Nike's physical doors in China), Adidas China keeps outperforming, and the niche/professional brand strategy (HOKA, Norrona, norda, Soar, Ciele, ektos stores) together with instant retail and private-domain channels for non-Nike brands backfills part of the online hole. With a China consumer recovery from FY2029, revenue returns to 3-4% growth off a ~RMB19.7bn base and the net-of-lease margin rebuilds to 8% (the FY2024 level was 10.5%).
scenario_narratives.bear: Nike's notice is the first of several: offline Nike terms are reset in Nike's favour (fewer and lower-tier doors, thinner margins), Adidas adopts the same online-direct model by FY2029, and Chinese discretionary spending stays soft. Revenue roughly halves to ~RMB12bn by FY2033, the net-of-lease EBITDA margin settles at ~3.5%, and the dividend is cut to what a RMB200-250m/yr cash business can pay. The value in this path is mostly the RMB1.2bn net cash plus the working capital that unwinds on the way down.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 35%: the business depends on two brand principals who together are ~87% of revenue and who can change distribution terms unilaterally, which Nike has just done for the online channel, and the offline Nike terms are unresolved as of the valuation date. That is a single-counterparty dependency with a live, unquantified adverse event -- the method's explicit trigger for a 25-35%+ bear weight. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right (Nike offline consolidation around Topsports, Adidas staying put, a China consumer recovery). Base 45%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Topsports is valued as a structurally shrinking, net-cash, zero-SBC sportswear distributor whose cash flows are controlled by two brand principals. The model deliberately does not assume a re-rating: every scenario has lower revenue in FY2036 than FY2026 except the bull (which returns to roughly FY2026 revenue only by FY2036), mature net-of-lease margins are set below the FY2022-24 range in all three cases, the terminal multiple is capped at 12x owner FCF, and leases are charged as an operating cost in the flows (treatment B) so the IFRS 16 financing-line flattery of reported FCF is removed. The Nike online termination is modelled explicitly in the year-1/year-2 revenue paths and the possibility that it spreads to Nike offline and to Adidas is carried by a 35% bear weight; the WACC carries only the permanent brand-principal dependency, not the event, so risk is charged once. Because inventory and receivables are 25% of revenue, the contraction itself throws off cash, and in the bear case that release plus net cash is most of the value. The stock trades near the bear-case value and well below the probability-weighted value; the gap is the price the market puts on the unresolved Nike offline terms and on a possible dividend cut.
key_risks_to_valuation: Nike offline cooperation terms (unresolved): a reset to fewer doors or thinner margins would push the base case toward the bear path; a confirmation on current terms would push it toward the bull.
Adidas (~30-35% of revenue) adopting Nike's online-direct approach -- this is in the bear case only.
H1 FY2027 interim (six months to 31 Aug 2026) not yet in the folder: the actual decline rate and margin print for the pre-cut-off period will re-anchor the FY2027 and FY2028 driver years.
Working-capital release assumption (-12% capture): if the Nike online inventory has to be cleared at deep markdowns or returned at a loss, the FY2027-28 cash release is smaller than modelled.

Dividend: >100% payout ratios (137% in FY2026) are funded partly from cash; the model values FCF not dividends, but a cut would move the market price and the hurdle entry price would then be the reference.
RMB/HKD: per-share values are converted at CNYHKD 1.1747 (2026-10-23); refresh_price.py does not update fx_rate, so the rate must be refreshed by hand on later price-only updates.
Terminal multiple: 12x cap on a business that may still be shrinking in year 10; Gordon binds in the base case at 1.5% growth, so the cap is a brake, not the driver.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (6110.HK) at inputs.price_as_of; HKEX regular close; 52-week range HK$0.93-3.50. FX: Yahoo CNYHKD=X at the same date.
data_sources.financials: 6110.HK_Metrics.csv (FY2019-FY2026 annuals, H1 FY2025/H1 FY2026 interims, exported from core_metrics); FY2026 annual report (year ended 28 Feb 2026) for net cash (Liquidity section), lease payments (cash flow statement, financing), D&A split (note 13 staff costs/expenses by nature: ROU depreciation 912.1, PP&E depreciation 366.4, amortization 15.6), finance costs note 9, inventories/receivables/payables (balance sheet notes 21/22/24), share count (Directors' report), EPS note 11.
data_sources.qualitative: 6110.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-24): Nike 22 July 2026 online-authorization termination effective 1 Jan 2027 (online Nike ~22% of FY2026 revenue), mid-2026 voluntary disclosure of a 10-20% sales decline, store count and margin history, brand concentration (Nike + Adidas ~87% of revenue).
